items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Well, I met him around in 1928 and 9, around Chicago, yeah.

ctx.x: Well, that's practically all we played. You'd have to play that style for people to dance by. On blues, except you played a mighty good beat, slow blues, because most of the time, Jooks, Balleisers, people danced, you know. Yeah. Well, that's mostly we played, but we didn't call it Pinetop's Boogie Woogie. We didn't call it Boogie Woogie at all. They called it Dudlow Joe.
Dudlow Joe. Dudlow Joe. That was the style of the bass, you mean, isn't it? That's right. Rolling bass and different types. Oh, Cal Cal Davenport, when did you first hear him or meet him?
Well, I met him around in 1928 and 9, around Chicago, yeah. What's it called? At the Old Angelus building now, 35th and Wabash. That's where we were located at the time. Of course, it's called now.
